state.task: Two agents analysed Java code for path traversal (CWE-22). Their final answers follow, then the code of each method in question.
agent_answers: {"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "Expand", "method": "extractFile", "explanation": "The untrusted archive entry name obtained from ZipEntry.getName() is used directly as a path component in FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) without adequate sanitization or containment checking, allowing an attacker to specify paths that escape the destination directory through directory traversal sequences like '../'. While there is a check using getAbsolutePath().startsWith(dir.getAbsolutePath()) after the file resolution, this check can be bypassed if the resolved file path is normalized or if the check is not performed correctly in all cases, making the path resolution vulnerable to path traversal attacks."}]}

{"findings": [{"cwe": "CWE-22", "class": "Expand", "method": "extractFile", "explanation": "In extractFile, the ZipEntry name obtained from ze.getName() reaches the FileOutputStream(File) sink through FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName). The only guard is `if ( !f.getAbsolutePath().startsWith( dir.getAbsolutePath() ) )`, which is an inadequate containment check because it does a raw string prefix comparison without path normalization or a trailing path-separator boundary; entries such as `../analysis-output-2` or absolute paths sharing the destination prefix pass the check and cause extraction outside the target directory."}]}
